rationale: B gives a clear recommendation tied to the actual decision options and explains why the phased setup fits different stages of the work. It provides comparative logic across alternatives, includes downside/worst-case framing, and references point estimates plus confidence intervals, which is materially useful. A is much less helpful: it recommends an apparent new option not in the original choice set, does not clearly identify the main alternative, and mostly lists KPIs rather than using them to discriminate among options. Its caveats and quantitative support are too thin to guide a careful decision-maker.
